# phase-115 — Check every GRAMMAR production against the parser, not just the keyword table

|---|---|

## You must change `tests/ or docs/`

This phase declares `must_touch: [tests/ or docs/]`. The gate fails the phase unless at
least one changed file falls under it. Writing tests, documentation or a report
is not enough — if you finish without touching that area, the phase fails on
exactly that check.


## Evidence — verified finding

```
tests/keyword_reservation_test.rs:21 does `const GRAMMAR: __FINDING__str = include_str!("../docs/GRAMMAR.md");` and its tests read exactly one thing out of it: the reserved-keyword list at docs/GRAMMAR.md:41-50, checked against `Lexer::keywords()`. Nothing in the 1,539-test suite checks any OTHER production in that file. That is the mechanism by which `else if` (phase-112), the whole type system (phase-113), multiple assignment and dotted import (phase-114) all shipped while the documentation promised them and the suite stayed green - three independent audits have now re-found this by hand. AGENTS.md section 2 treats docs/GRAMMAR.md as part of the language contract ('Existing tests in tests/ keep passing', 'Full grammar: docs/GRAMMAR.md'), so a production that does not parse is not a documentation nit, it is a promise the project cannot keep, and nothing currently notices.
```

**Re-verify this before you change anything.** If the finding no longer
reproduces on `main`, stop and write that to `FINDINGS.md` — a stale phase must
never be "fixed" by inventing a change.

## Goal

Extend the existing GRAMMAR conformance guard so that every EBNF production in docs/GRAMMAR.md is checked against the parser - accepted, or explicitly marked Not Implemented - instead of only the keyword table.

## Method

1. Read `AGENTS.md` in full. Obey every hard rule; they are not negotiable.
2. Reproduce the finding. Record the exact command and the exact wrong output.
3. Write the failing test FIRST. Watch it fail. Do not touch production code
   until you have a red test that fails for the right reason.
4. Make the smallest change that turns it green.
5. Run the four gates yourself before claiming anything:

   ```bash
   cargo fmt --all -- --check
   cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
   cargo test --all-targets
   ./rbops/verify.sh phase-115
   ```

6. Write `REPORT.md` in the exact shape required by `AGENTS.md` section 4.

## Definition of done

- [ ] a test enumerates the EBNF productions in docs/GRAMMAR.md and asserts each one is either exercised by a program that parses or carries a Not Implemented marker - so a production cannot be neither
- [ ] adding a new production to docs/GRAMMAR.md without a test and without the marker fails `cargo test`, proven by a checked-in negative case
- [ ] a production marked Not Implemented is asserted to be REFUSED by the built parser, so the marker cannot go stale into a lie
- [ ] the keyword-table check already at tests/keyword_reservation_test.rs still passes and is kept, not replaced
- [ ] the guard covers at least sections 2 (types), 4.1 (declarations), 4.3 (control flow) and 5 (expressions) of docs/GRAMMAR.md, and the audit report names which sections are still uncovered
- [ ] `cargo test` reports 0 failures and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean
